answer:
Research papers on multi-agent orchestration span three primary areas: foundational survey taxonomies, core coordination frameworks, and empirical evaluation benchmarks.

### Surveys and Architectural Taxonomies
- [Large Language Model based Multi-Agents: A Survey of Progress and Challenges](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01680) (Guo et al., 2024). Surveys architectural challenges, multi-agent collaboration mechanisms, complex problem-solving workflows, and world simulation environments.
- [Beyond Self-Talk: A Communication-Centric Survey of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14321) (Yan et al., 2025, *Frontiers of Computer Science*). Classifies message-passing topologies, interaction structures, and inter-agent coordination protocols.
- [Large Language Models in the Loop: A Stability- and Network-Aware Survey in Networked Control, Cyber-Physical, and Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16599) (Du & Chan, 2026). Analyzes multi-agent orchestration under network constraints, stability criteria, and closed-loop control dynamics.

### Core Orchestration Frameworks
- [AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155) (Wu et al., 2023). Introduces conversable agent graphs supporting hierarchical, group chat, and programmable multi-party routing.
- [MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352) (Hong et al., 2023). Implements assembly-line orchestration by encoding Standardized Operating Procedures (SOPs) into structured prompt sequences.
- [CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17760) (Li et al., 2023). Establishes autonomous peer-to-peer task execution using inception prompting and bilateral role-play coordination.

### Benchmarks, Consensus Protocols, and Failure Dynamics
- [SwarmBench: Can Large Language Models Act as Agent Swarm Orchestrators?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30661) (Gao et al., 2026). Evaluates LLMs acting as dynamic orchestrators over agent swarms; highlights execution quality gaps and mitigates failure modes using experience replay (SwarmExp).
- [LLM-Coordination: Evaluating and Analyzing Multi-agent Coordination Abilities in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.03903.pdf) (Agashe et al., 2023). Tests decentralized consensus and coordination dynamics in pure coordination games without central supervisors.
- [Silo-Bench: A Scalable Environment for Evaluating Distributed Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Silo-Bench%3A-A-Scalable-Environment-for-Evaluating-Zhang-Liu/4d94b0a424264ea5ea7fa7df87f3ddbceee35070) (Zhang et al., 2026). Evaluates communication scaling bottlenecks; finds that increasing agent count fails to overcome context limitations.
- [How Much Coordination Gain Is Real? A Paired Noise-Floor Protocol for Multi-Agent LLM Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.20695.pdf) (Kaliyev & Maryanskyy, 2026). Evaluates illusory coordination improvements; defines a paired noise-floor audit metric (`pass^k` restricted to trials where coordination logic is actively executed).
- [Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.08340.pdf) (Tessera et al., 2026). Introduces the Alem environment to quantify bottlenecks in dynamic role assignment, plan execution, and communication load.

### Missing and Uncertain Information
- Google Scholar bot detection blocked citation count retrieval across all papers; relative citation rank cannot be confirmed.
- Action execution limits halted retrieval before collecting paper metadata for ChatDev (`arXiv:2307.07924`) and graph-based workflow engines (such as LangGraph).
- Quantitative ablation tables, token usage breakdowns, and exact latency metrics for benchmarks like SwarmBench were not extracted.

- [MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352) | **Authors:** Sirui Hong, Mingchen Zhuge, Jiaqi Chen, Xiawu Zheng, Yuheng Cheng, Ceyao Zhang, Jinlin Wang, Zili Wang, Steven Ka Shing Yau, Zijuan Lin, Liyang Zhou, Chenyu Ran, Lingfeng Xiao, Chenglin Wu, Jürgen Schmidhuber | **Year:** 2023 | **Framework Name:** MetaGPT | **Orchestration Pattern:** Role-scoped assembly line / Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) sequential and workflow-based routing | **Evidence:** Abstract states it introduces a meta-programming framework incorporating human workflows by encoding Standardized Operating Procedures (SOPs) into prompt sequences, assigning diverse roles across an assembly line paradigm to break down complex tasks. | **Relevance:** Primary multi-agent system structuring LLM coordination via standardized procedural roles rather than freeform dialogue.
- [CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17760) | **Authors:** Guohao Li, Hasan Abed Al Kader Hammoud, Hani Itani, Dmitrii Khizbullin, Bernard Ghanem | **Year:** 2023 | **Framework Name:** CAMEL | **Orchestration Pattern:** Autonomous bilateral role-playing via inception prompting (peer-to-peer communicative coordination) | **Evidence:** Abstract notes it proposes a novel communicative agent framework named role-playing using inception prompting to guide chat agents toward autonomous task completion while maintaining consistency without human intervention. | **Relevance:** Seminal early framework establishing peer-to-peer agent-to-agent communication protocols and inception prompting for autonomous multi-agent task execution.

- Hit tool budget before extracting the details for ChatDev (`2307.07924`) and graph-based execution engines (e.g., LangGraph). Citation counts could not be verified on-page and remain unverified.

- [How Much Coordination Gain Is Real? A Paired Noise-Floor Protocol for Multi-Agent LLM Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.20695.pdf) | **Authors:** Alibek T. Kaliyev, Artem Maryanskyy | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark name:** Paired Noise-Floor Protocol | **Evaluated metrics:** Coordination-active $pass^k$, runtime overhead, empirical gain vs. noise floor | **Key findings:** Discloses that nominal multi-agent coordination gains on standard benchmarks often reflect noise rather than genuine multi-agent orchestration improvements; introduces an auditing protocol restricting evaluations to trials where coordination mechanisms are active. | **Evidence:** Record states: "defines coordination-active pass^k, pass^k restricted to trials where the coordination mechanism is logically active, as the minimum reporting protocol, with sample-size targets and runtime hooks in the body". | **Relevance:** Addresses failure modes, illusory coordination gains, and evaluation rigor in multi-agent orchestration benchmarks.
- [Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.08340.pdf) | **Authors:** K. Tessera, A. Szécsényi, et al., A. Storkey | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark name:** Alem | **Evaluated metrics:** Shared plan execution rate, role allocation accuracy, communication volume | **Key findings:** Provides a JAX-based environment designed to quantify coordination bottlenecks in language agents that must communicate, assign roles dynamically, and execute shared plans. | **Evidence:** Record states: "Alem is introduced, a JAX-based benchmark for open-ended multi-agent coordination... that makes this bottleneck measurable and provides a controlled testbed for developing agents that communicate, allocate roles, and execute shared plans." | **Relevance:** Evaluates dynamic role allocation, communication bottlenecks, and plan execution in multi-agent settings.

- [AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155) | **Authors:** Qingyun Wu, Gagan Bansal, Jieyu Zhang, Yiran Wu, Beibin Li, Erkang Zhu, Li Jiang, Xiaoyun Zhang, Shaokun Zhang, Jiale Liu, Ahmed Hassan Awadallah, Ryen W White, Doug Burger, Chi Wang | **Year:** 2023 | **Framework Name:** AutoGen | **Orchestration Pattern:** Conversable multi-agent routing (supports hierarchical, group chat, and programmable multi-party conversation graphs) | **Evidence:** Abstract states AutoGen is an open-source framework allowing developers to build LLM applications via multiple agents that converse to accomplish tasks, defining interaction behaviors via natural language and code to program flexible conversation patterns. | **Relevance:** Foundational multi-agent execution framework providing generalized conversational orchestration across arbitrary agent topologies.
- [MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352) | **Authors:** Sirui Hong, Mingchen Zhuge, Jiaqi Chen, Xiawu Zheng, Yuheng Cheng, Ceyao Zhang, Jinlin Wang, Zili Wang, Steven Ka Shing Yau, Zijuan Lin, Liyang Zhou, Chenyu Ran, Lingfeng Xiao, Chenglin Wu, Jürgen Schmidhuber | **Year:** 2023 | **Framework Name:** MetaGPT | **Orchestration Pattern:** Role-scoped assembly line / Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) sequential and workflow-based routing | **Evidence:** Abstract states it introduces a meta-programming framework incorporating human workflows by encoding Standardized Operating Procedures (SOPs) into prompt sequences, assigning diverse roles across an assembly line paradigm to break down complex tasks. | **Relevance:** Primary multi-agent system structuring LLM coordination via standardized procedural roles rather than freeform dialogue.
- [CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17760) | **Authors:** Guohao Li, Hasan Abed Al Kader Hammoud, Hani Itani, Dmitrii Khizbullin, Bernard Ghanem | **Year:** 2023 | **Framework Name:** CAMEL | **Orchestration Pattern:** Autonomous bilateral role-playing via inception prompting (peer-to-peer communicative coordination) | **Evidence:** Abstract notes it proposes a novel communicative agent framework named role-playing using inception prompting to guide chat agents toward autonomous task completion while maintaining consistency without human intervention. | **Relevance:** Seminal early framework establishing peer-to-peer agent-to-agent communication protocols and inception prompting for autonomous multi-agent task execution.

### Coverage
- Google Scholar: Attempted entry query `https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22multi-agent%22+orchestration+framework+LLM+architecture` (blocked by bot detection check).
- arXiv: Queried `"multi-agent" orchestration framework LLM` (333 total results returned, reviewed first page of recent works) and inspected foundational repository papers directly (`2308.08155`, `2308.00352`, `2303.17760`, `2307.07924`).

### Limitations
- Google Scholar blocked automated access with a bot detection challenge, preventing direct retrieval of citation counts from Scholar.
- Hit tool budget before extracting the details for ChatDev (`2307.07924`) and graph-based execution engines (e.g., LangGraph). Citation counts could not be verified on-page and remain unverified.

benchmarks_and_coordination_dynamics.findings:
### Findings
- [SwarmBench: Can Large Language Models Act as Agent Swarm Orchestrators?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30661) | **Authors:** Jinshan Gao, Zhuoran Jin, Tianyi Men, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark name:** SwarmBench | **Evaluated metrics:** Accuracy, efficiency, cost, process quality | **Key findings:** Evaluates LLMs acting dynamically as orchestrators over agent swarms instead of fixed topologies; models exhibit substantial capability gaps in coordination efficiency and process execution quality. Proposes SwarmExp (experience extraction and replay) to mitigate orchestration failure modes and bottlenecks. | **Evidence:** Page abstract states: "propose SwarmBench, a benchmark that evaluates model performance from multiple perspectives, including accuracy, efficiency, cost, and process quality... current models exhibit substantial differences in orchestration capability... reflected not only in final accuracy, efficiency, and cost, but also in the overall quality of the orchestration process itself." | **Relevance:** Directly evaluates orchestration bottlenecks, efficiency, cost, and process failure modes in dynamic multi-agent swarms.
- [LLM-Coordination: Evaluating and Analyzing Multi-agent Coordination Abilities in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.03903.pdf) | **Authors:** S. Agashe, Yue Fan, Anthony Reyna, Xin Eric Wang | **Year:** 2023 | **Benchmark name:** LLM-Coordination Benchmark | **Evaluated metrics:** Coordination success rate, payoff maximization, communication efficiency | **Key findings:** Establishes pure coordination game environments to assess whether LLM agents can reach consensus and coordinate decentralized actions without centralized overseers or conflict of interest. | **Evidence:** Paper record states: "The LLM-Coordination Benchmark is introduced, a novel benchmark for analyzing LLMs in the context of Pure Coordination Settings, where agents must cooperate to maximize gains." | **Relevance:** Benchmark measuring multi-agent consensus protocols and coordination dynamics under cooperative game conditions.
- [Silo-Bench: A Scalable Environment for Evaluating Distributed Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Silo-Bench%3A-A-Scalable-Environment-for-Evaluating-Zhang-Liu/4d94b0a424264ea5ea7fa7df87f3ddbceee35070) | **Authors:** Yu-Zhe Zhang, Fei-Ran Liu, et al., Wen-Yuan Jiang | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark name:** SILO-BENCH | **Evaluated metrics:** Task completion, communication complexity scaling, context efficiency | **Key findings:** Analyzes multi-agent coordination across 30 algorithmic tasks with three levels of communication complexity; reveals that naively scaling the agent count fails to resolve coordination bottlenecks due to context limitations. | **Evidence:** Page TLDR states: "SILO-BENCH, a role-agnostic benchmark of 30 algorithmic tasks across three communication complexity levels, is introduced, demonstrating that naively scaling agent count cannot circumvent context limitations". | **Relevance:** Evaluates communication overhead, coordination scaling bottlenecks, and context limit failures in multi-agent orchestration.
- [How Much Coordination Gain Is Real? A Paired Noise-Floor Protocol for Multi-Agent LLM Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.20695.pdf) | **Authors:** Alibek T. Kaliyev, Artem Maryanskyy | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark name:** Paired Noise-Floor Protocol | **Evaluated metrics:** Coordination-active $pass^k$, runtime overhead, empirical gain vs. noise floor | **Key findings:** Discloses that nominal multi-agent coordination gains on standard benchmarks often reflect noise rather than genuine multi-agent orchestration improvements; introduces an auditing protocol restricting evaluations to trials where coordination mechanisms are active. | **Evidence:** Record states: "defines coordination-active pass^k, pass^k restricted to trials where the coordination mechanism is logically active, as the minimum reporting protocol, with sample-size targets and runtime hooks in the body". | **Relevance:** Addresses failure modes, illusory coordination gains, and evaluation rigor in multi-agent orchestration benchmarks.
- [Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.08340.pdf) | **Authors:** K. Tessera, A. Szécsényi, et al., A. Storkey | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark name:** Alem | **Evaluated metrics:** Shared plan execution rate, role allocation accuracy, communication volume | **Key findings:** Provides a JAX-based environment designed to quantify coordination bottlenecks in language agents that must communicate, assign roles dynamically, and execute shared plans. | **Evidence:** Record states: "Alem is introduced, a JAX-based benchmark for open-ended multi-agent coordination... that makes this bottleneck measurable and provides a controlled testbed for developing agents that communicate, allocate roles, and execute shared plans." | **Relevance:** Evaluates dynamic role allocation, communication bottlenecks, and plan execution in multi-agent settings.

### Coverage
- **Sites searched:** Google Scholar (blocked by CAPTCHA), arXiv search, Semantic Scholar.
- **Queries executed:**
  - Google Scholar: `"multi-agent" orchestration benchmark evaluation LLM`
  - arXiv: `"multi-agent" benchmark evaluation orchestration`
  - arXiv: `"multi-agent" AND "benchmark" AND ("orchestration" OR "coordination" OR "failure" OR "consensus")`
  - Semantic Scholar: `multi-agent coordination benchmark LLM`
- **Results reviewed:** Approximately 60 search results across arXiv and Semantic Scholar listings.

### Limitations
- Google Scholar blocked automated access with a robot verification challenge.
- Browser action limit (10 actions) stopped further direct retrieval from Papers with Code and detailed full-text metric scraping for individual ablation tables.
- Exact breakdown of token consumption and numeric latency for individual models within SwarmBench could not be extracted before halting.
